risks: Clinical risks of titration (hyperkalaemia, hypotension, kidney injury) managed by the protocol's hold and referral rules; no research procedures are added.
consent: Patients consent to treatment in the usual clinical way; monitoring uses routine clinical data under the registered service evaluation, with an information leaflet describing the measures.
data: Measures are held in the service's restricted spreadsheet without names; monthly reports show counts only.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: deprivation, distance, age over 80, language and hearing are expected to affect attendance. Telephone and clinic visits are both offered, blood tests can be taken at community sites, interpreters are booked for visits, and missed visits and doses reached are reported by deprivation fifth.
effectiveness: Success is at least 60 percent at half target dose or more at 6 months with balancing measures within the expected rates.
efficiency: Uses existing nurse prescriber time; reduces titration-only consultant appointments.
costs: Nurse time within the service establishment; blood tests already funded.
partnerships: Cardiology clinical lead, community phlebotomy service, primary care practices for shared results, two patient partners from the heart failure support group.
rebPath: Registered with clinical governance as a service evaluation (SE-2026-044); no research ethics review is required under the trust's policy because no research question is tested and no extra data are collected.
limitations: No comparison group; referral selection; tests done in primary care may be missed.
summary: Routine clinical consent, a registered service evaluation, and equity measures built into visit options and reporting.
